text: Let the foci of a hyperbola $H$ coincide with the foci of the ellipse $E:\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{100}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{75}=1$ and the eccentricity of the hyperbola $H$ be the reciprocal of the eccentricity of the ellipse $E$. If the length of the transverse axis of $H$ is $α$ and the length of its conjugate axis is $β$, then $3α^{2}+2β^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$E:\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{100}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{75}=1$

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{Eccentricity of ellipse,}e_{E} & =\sqrt{1-\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}} \\ =\sqrt{1-\dfrac{75}{100}} \\ e_{E}=\dfrac{1}{2} \end{array}$

$\therefore e_{H}=2$ [ as eccentricity of hyperbola is reciprocal of eccentricity of ellipse]

Transverse axis of hyperbola $=α$

Conjugate axis of hyperbola $=β$

Also, foci of ellipse $(1\pm ae,1)$

$\begin{array}{l} =\left (1\pm \left (10\times \dfrac{1}{2}\right ),1\right ) \\ =(1\pm 5,1) \\ =(6,1)\text{and}(-4,1) \end{array}$

Distance between foci $=10$

$\begin{array}{l} 2ae=10 \\ \Rightarrow a=\dfrac{5}{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{llll} \text{also,}e^{2}=1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} \\ \begin{array}{ll} 4 & =1+\dfrac{4b^{2}}{25} \\ b^{2} & =\dfrac{75}{4} \\ b & =\dfrac{\sqrt{75}}{2} \end{array} \\ \Rightarrow α=5 \\ \text{and}β=\sqrt{75} \\ 3α^{2}+2β^{2}=3(5)^{2}+2(75)=225 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}-\sqrt{2}x-\sqrt{3}=0 \\ P_{n}=α^{n}-β^{n} \end{array}$

$α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation

Using Newton's theorem

$\begin{array}{l} P_{n+2}-\sqrt{2}P_{n+1}-\sqrt{3}P_{n}=0 \\ \text{Put}n=10 \\ P_{12}-\sqrt{2}P_{11}-\sqrt{3}P_{10}=0 \end{array}$

text: If an unbiased dice is rolled thrice, then the probability of getting a greater number in the $i^{\text{th}}$ roll than the number obtained in the $(i-1)^{\text{th}}$ roll, $i=2,3$, is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's denote the outcomes of the three rolls as $X_{1}$, $X_{2}$, and $X_{3}$, where $X_{i}$ represents the number obtained in the $i^{\text{th}}$ roll. We are looking for the probability that:

$X_{2}>X_{1}\text{and}X_{3}>X_{2}$

The total number of outcomes when rolling a dice three times is: 

$6^{3}=216$

Let's count the favorable outcomes. For each satisfying outcome, we must ensure that both inequalities are adhered to. Consider the possible sequences where every subsequent roll's number is higher than the previous roll's number. These sequences are:

(1, 2, 3)

(1, 2, 4)

(1, 2, 5)

(1, 2, 6)

(1, 3, 4)

(1, 3, 5)

(1, 3, 6)

(1, 4, 5)

(1, 4, 6)

(1, 5, 6)

(2, 3, 4)

(2, 3, 5)

(2, 3, 6)

(2, 4, 5)

(2, 4, 6)

(2, 5, 6)

(3, 4, 5)

(3, 4, 6)

(3, 5, 6)

(4, 5, 6)

Clearly, there are 20 such favorable outcomes. Hence, the probability is given by:

$\frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total number of outcomes}}=\frac{20}{216}=\frac{5}{54}$

Therefore, the correct option is:

Option A: $\frac{5}{54}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: The value of the integral $\int\limits _{-1}^{2}\log _{e}\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right )dx$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g(x)=\log _{e}\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right )$ is odd, since $g(-x)=\log _{e}\left (\sqrt{x^{2}+1}-x\right )=\log _{e}\dfrac{1}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}=-g(x)$. So $\int\limits _{-1}^{1}g(x)dx=0$ and

$I=\int\limits _{1}^{2}\log _{e}\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right )dx$

With $g^{'}(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}$, integration by parts gives

$\int g(x)dx=xg(x)-\int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}dx=x\log _{e}\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right )-\sqrt{x^{2}+1}$

$I=\left [2\log _{e}\left (2+\sqrt{5}\right )-\sqrt{5}\right ]-\left [\log _{e}\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )-\sqrt{2}\right ]=\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{5}+\log _{e}\dfrac{\left (2+\sqrt{5}\right )^{2}}{1+\sqrt{2}}$

Since $\left (2+\sqrt{5}\right )^{2}=9+4\sqrt{5}$, $I=\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{5}+\log _{e}\left (\dfrac{9+4\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{2}}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 35=14|⃗{r}|^{2} \\ \Rightarrow |⃗{r}|=\sqrt{\dfrac{35}{14}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\neq \sqrt{10} \end{array}$

$\text{(i.e.,}\cos 2A+\cos 2B+\cos 2C\geq -\frac{3}{2}\text{)}$

and $|OA\leftarrow |^{2}=|OB\leftarrow |^{2}=|OC\leftarrow |^{2}=R^{2}\text{..... (2)}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 3R^{2}+2R^{2}(\cos 2A+\cos 2B+\cos 2C)\geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow \cos 2A+\cos 2B+\cos 2C\geq -\dfrac{3}{2} \end{array}$

text: Let $B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ]$ and $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix such that $AB^{-1}=A^{-1}$. If $BCB^{-1}=A$ and $C^{4}+αC^{2}+βI=O$, then $2β-α$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lll} B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ] \\ AB^{-1}=A^{-1} \\ \Rightarrow A^{2}=B \end{array}$

Also, $BCB^{-1}=A$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow C & =B^{-1}AB \\ \Rightarrow C^{4} & =\left (B^{-1}AB\right )\left (B^{-1}AB\right )\left (B^{-1}AB\right )\left (B^{-1}AB\right ) \\ =B^{-1}A^{4}B \\ =B^{-1}B^{2}B \\ \Rightarrow \quad C^{4} & =B^{2} \end{array}$

Also, $C^{2}=\left (B^{-1}AB\right )\left (B^{-1}AB\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} =B^{-1}A^{2}B \\ =B^{-1}BB \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllllllll} \Rightarrow C^{2}=B \\ \Rightarrow C^{4}+αC^{2}+βI=0 \\ \Rightarrow B^{2}+αB+βI=0 \\ B^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & 18 \\ 6 & 28 \end{array}\right ] \\ \Rightarrow \left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & 18 \\ 6 & 28 \end{array}\right ]+α\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 0 \\ 0 & β \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ] \\ \Rightarrow 4+α+β=0 \end{array}$

and $18+3α=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow α=-6 \\ \Rightarrow β=2 \\ \Rightarrow 2β-α=10 \end{array}$

text: $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{e-(1+2x)^{\dfrac{1}{2x}}}{x}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $t=2x$, so $t\to 0$. Then $(1+t)^{1/t}=e^{\frac{\ln (1+t)}{t}}$ with $\dfrac{\ln (1+t)}{t}=1-\dfrac{t}{2}+\dfrac{t^{2}}{3}-\ldots$

So $(1+t)^{1/t}=e\cdot e^{-\frac{t}{2}+O(t^{2})}=e\left (1-\dfrac{t}{2}\right )+O(t^{2})$.

Putting $t=2x$: $(1+2x)^{\frac{1}{2x}}=e-ex+O(x^{2})$.

Therefore

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{e-(1+2x)^{\dfrac{1}{2x}}}{x}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{ex+O(x^{2})}{x}=e.$

The $1^{\infty }$ rule only gives $(1+2x)^{\frac{1}{2x}}\to e$, which makes the numerator tend to 0 together with the denominator; it does not make the limit 0.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: Let $a,ar,ar^{2}$, ............ be an infinite G.P. If $\sum\limits _{n=0}^{\infty }ar^{n}=57$ and $\sum\limits _{n=0}^{\infty }a^{3}r^{3n}=9747$, then $a+18r$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text: The sum of the coefficients of $x^{2/3}$ and $x^{-2/5}$ in the binomial expansion of $\left (x^{2/3}+\frac{1}{2}x^{-2/5}\right )^{9}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} T_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left (\dfrac{x^{-2/5}}{2}\right )^{r}\left (x^{2/3}\right )^{9-r} \\ ={}^{9}C_{r}\dfrac{1}{2^{r}}x^{\frac{2}{3}(9-r)+\left (\frac{-2r}{5}\right )} \\ ={}^{9}C_{r}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2^{r}}\cdot x^{6-\frac{16r}{15}} \end{array}$

For coefficient of $x^{2/3}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 6-\dfrac{16r}{15}=\dfrac{2}{3} \\ \Rightarrow 90-16r=10 \\ \Rightarrow r=5 \end{array}$

For coefficient of $x^{-2/5}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 6-\dfrac{16r}{15}=\dfrac{-2}{5} \\ \Rightarrow 90-16r=-6 \\ \Rightarrow r=6 \end{array}$

Sum of coefficients of $x^{2/3}$ & $x^{-2/5}$

$\begin{array}{l} ={}^{9}C_{5}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2^{5}}+{}^{9}C_{6}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2^{6}} \\ =\dfrac{9!}{5!4!}\left (\dfrac{1}{2^{5}}\right )+\dfrac{9!}{6!3!}\left (\dfrac{1}{2^{6}}\right )=\dfrac{21}{4} \end{array}$

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+α\hat{j}+\hat{k},⃗{b}=-\hat{i}+\hat{k},⃗{c}=β\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, where $α$ and $β$ are integers and $αβ=-6$. Let the values of the ordered pair $(α,β)$, for which the area of the parallelogram of diagonals $⃗{a}+⃗{b}$ and $⃗{b}+⃗{c}$ is $\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}$, be $(α_{1},β_{1})$ and $(α_{2},β_{2})$. Then $α_{1}^{2}+β_{1}^{2}-α_{2}β_{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Area of parallelogram whose diagonals are $⃗{a}+⃗{b}$ and $⃗{b}+⃗{c}$ is

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{1}{2}|(⃗{a}+⃗{b})\times (⃗{b}+⃗{c})| \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}|⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}+⃗{a}\times ⃗{c}+⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}| \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}|-2β\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+(α+β)\hat{k}| \end{array}$

$=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4β^{2}+4+(α+β)^{2}}$

Which is given $\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore  & 4β^{2}+4+(α+β)^{2}=21 \\ \Rightarrow  & (α+β)^{2}+4β^{2}=17 \\ \Rightarrow  & α^{2}+5β^{2}+2αβ=17 \\ \Rightarrow  & α^{2}+5β^{2}=29 \\ \therefore  & (α,β)\in \{(3,2),(-3,-2),(-3,2),(3,-2)\} \\ \because  & αβ=-6 \\ \therefore  & (α,β)\in \{(-3,2),(3,-2)\} \\ \therefore  & α_{1}^{2}+β_{1}^{2}-α_{2}β_{2} \\ = & 9+4-(-6)=19 \end{array}$

text: Consider the matrices : $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -5 \\ 3 & m \end{array}\right ],B=\left [\begin{array}{l} 20 \\ m \end{array}\right ]$ and $X=\left [\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \end{array}\right ]$. Let the set of all $m$, for which the system of equations $AX=B$ has a negative solution (i.e., $x<0$ and $y<0$), be the interval $(a,b)$. Then $8\int\limits _{a}^{b}|A|dm$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} AX=B \\ 2x-5y=20 \\ 3x+my=m \\ \Rightarrow 3\left (\dfrac{20+5y}{2}\right )+my=m \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 30+\dfrac{15}{2}y+my=m \\ \Rightarrow y\left (\dfrac{15}{2}+m\right )=m-30 \\ \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{m-30}{\frac{15}{2}+m}<0\Rightarrow m\in \left (-\dfrac{15}{2},30\right ) \end{array}$

Similarly : $3x+m\left (\frac{2x-20}{5}\right )=m$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 3x+\dfrac{2mx}{5}-\dfrac{20m}{5}=m \\ \Rightarrow  & \dfrac{15x+2mx}{5}=5m\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{25m}{15+2m} \\ x<0\Rightarrow \dfrac{25m}{15+2m}<0\Rightarrow m\in \left (-\dfrac{15}{2},0\right ) \\ \therefore  & m\in \left (-\dfrac{15}{2},0\right ) \\ a=-\dfrac{15}{2},b=0 \\ 8\int\limits _{-\frac{15}{2}}^{0}(2m+15)dm=450 \end{array}$

text: For a differentiable function $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$, suppose $f^{'}(x)=3f(x)+α$, where $α\in \mathrm{ℝ},f(0)=1$ and $\lim _{x\to -\infty }f(x)=7$. Then $9f(-\log _{e}3)$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The equation $f^{'}(x)-3f(x)=α$ is linear with integrating factor $e^{-3x}$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left (f(x)e^{-3x}\right )=αe^{-3x}\Rightarrow f(x)e^{-3x}=-\dfrac{α}{3}e^{-3x}+C\Rightarrow f(x)=-\dfrac{α}{3}+Ce^{3x}.$

As $x\to -\infty$, $e^{3x}\to 0$, so $\lim _{x\to -\infty }f(x)=-\dfrac{α}{3}=7$, giving $α=-21$.

Then $f(0)=7+C=1$, so $C=-6$ and $f(x)=7-6e^{3x}$.

$f(-\log _{e}3)=7-6e^{-3\log _{e}3}=7-\dfrac{6}{27}=\dfrac{61}{9}\Rightarrow 9f(-\log _{e}3)=61.$

Hence, the answer is 61.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: Consider the circle $C:x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ and the parabola $P:y^{2}=8x$. If the set of all values of $α$, for which three chords of the circle $C$ on three distinct lines passing through the point $(α,0)$ are bisected by the parabola $P$ is the interval $(p,q)$, then $(2q-p)^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The midpoint of each chord lies on $P$, so it is $M(2t^{2},4t)$, and it must lie inside the circle $C$.

The chord of $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ with midpoint $(h,k)$ is $T=S_{1}$, i.e. $hx+ky=h^{2}+k^{2}$. For $M$ this is $2t^{2}x+4ty=4t^{4}+16t^{2}$.

The chord passes through $(α,0)$:

$2t^{2}α=4t^{4}+16t^{2}$

For $t=0$ the midpoint is the centre $(0,0)$ and the chord is the diameter along the $x$-axis, which passes through $(α,0)$ for every $α$. This gives one line.

For $t\neq 0$, $α=2t^{2}+8$, i.e. $t^{2}=\dfrac{α-8}{2}$. The values $t$ and $-t$ give two more distinct lines only when $t^{2}>0$, i.e. $α>8$.

The midpoint must lie inside the circle:

$4t^{4}+16t^{2}<4\Rightarrow (t^{2})^{2}+4t^{2}-1<0\Rightarrow t^{2}<\sqrt{5}-2$

So $α=2t^{2}+8<4+2\sqrt{5}$. Hence $α\in \left (8,4+2\sqrt{5}\right )$, giving $p=8$ and $q=4+2\sqrt{5}$.

$(2q-p)^{2}=\left (8+4\sqrt{5}-8\right )^{2}=(4\sqrt{5})^{2}=80$

Hence, the answer is 80.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: The square of the distance of the image of the point $(6,1,5)$ in the line $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z-2}{4}$, from the origin is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The line $\dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{4}$ has direction $(3,2,4)$; a general point on it is $A(3λ+1,2λ,4λ+2)$.

For $A$ to be the foot of the perpendicular from $P(6,1,5)$, the vector $PA\leftarrow =(3λ-5,2λ-1,4λ-3)$ must be perpendicular to $(3,2,4)$:

$3(3λ-5)+2(2λ-1)+4(4λ-3)=0\Rightarrow 29λ-29=0\Rightarrow λ=1$

So the foot is $A(4,2,6)$.

The foot is the midpoint of $P$ and its image $P^{'}$, so $P^{'}=2A-P=(8-6,4-1,12-5)=(2,3,7)$.

$OP^{'2}=2^{2}+3^{2}+7^{2}=4+9+49=62$

Hence, the answer is 62.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: Let the set of all values of $p$, for which $f(x)=\left (p^{2}-6p+8\right )\left (\sin ^{2}2x-\cos ^{2}2x\right )+2(2-p)x+7$ does not have any critical point, be the interval $(a,b)$. Then $16ab$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\sin ^{2}2x-\cos ^{2}2x=-\cos 4x$ and $p^{2}-6p+8=(p-2)(p-4)$,

$f(x)=-(p-2)(p-4)\cos 4x-2(p-2)x+7$

$f^{'}(x)=4(p-2)(p-4)\sin 4x-2(p-2)$

$f$ is differentiable everywhere, so it has no critical point exactly when $f^{'}(x)\neq 0$ for every real $x$.

As $\sin 4x$ takes every value in $[-1,1]$, $f^{'}(x)$ takes every value from $-2(p-2)-4|(p-2)(p-4)|$ to $-2(p-2)+4|(p-2)(p-4)|$. This range misses $0$ exactly when

$2|p-2|>4|p-2||p-4|$

For $p=2$ both sides are $0$ ($f$ is the constant $7$ and every point is critical), so $p\neq 2$. Dividing by $2|p-2|$:

$|p-4|<\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{7}{2}<p<\dfrac{9}{2}$

So $a=\dfrac{7}{2}$, $b=\dfrac{9}{2}$ and

$16ab=16\times \dfrac{63}{4}=252$

Hence, the answer is 252.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: The number of integers, between 100 and 1000 having the sum of their digits equal to 14 , is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An integer between 100 and 1000 with digit sum 14 is a three-digit number $abc–$ with $a\in \{1,2,\ldots ,9\}$, $b,c\in \{0,1,\ldots ,9\}$ and $b+c=14-a$.

The number of digit pairs $(b,c)$ with $b+c=s$ is $s+1$ for $0\leq s\leq 9$, and $19-s$ for $10\leq s\leq 18$ (then $b$ runs from $s-9$ to 9).

For $a=1,2,3,4$: $s=13,12,11,10$, giving $6,7,8,9$ pairs.

For $a=5,6,7,8,9$: $s=9,8,7,6,5$, giving $10,9,8,7,6$ pairs.

Total $=6+7+8+9+10+9+8+7+6=70$.

Hence, the answer is 70.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift

text: If $\left (\frac{1}{α+1}+\frac{1}{α+2}+\ldots ..+\frac{1}{α+1012}\right )-\left (\frac{1}{2\cdot 1}+\frac{1}{4\cdot 3}+\frac{1}{6\cdot 5}+\ldots \ldots +\frac{1}{2024\cdot 2023}\right )=\frac{1}{2024}$, then $α$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{α+1}+\dfrac{1}{α+2}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{α+1012}- \\ \left (\dfrac{1}{2\times 1}+\dfrac{1}{4\times 3}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{2024}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2023}\right )=\dfrac{1}{2024} \\ \sum\limits _{r=1}^{1012}\dfrac{1}{2r(2r-1)}=\sum\limits _{r=1}^{1012}\left (\dfrac{1}{2r-1}-\dfrac{1}{2r}\right ) \\ =\left (1-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right )+\ldots +\left (\dfrac{1}{2023}-\dfrac{1}{2024}\right ) \\ =\left (1+\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{5}+\ldots .+\dfrac{1}{2023}\right ) \\ -\left (\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{1}{6}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{2024}\right ) \\ =\left (1+\dfrac{1}{3}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{2023}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{3}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{1012}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\left (1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{3}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{2023}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{1011}\right ) \\ \dfrac{-1}{2}\left (1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{1012}\right ) \\ =\dfrac{1}{1012}+\dfrac{1}{1013}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{2023}-\dfrac{1}{2024} \\ \Rightarrow α+1012=2023 \\ \Rightarrow α=1011 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 9th April Evening Shift
